claims.text: The funding is for seed-funding small grants.
The grants are for projects that bring the UK and Japan together.
The projects aim to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas/expertise, or build collaboration.
The funding is open to any field, including arts and culture, humanities, Japanese language, medicine and health, science, youth and education, and sport.
The UK office runs three award rounds a year.

records.justification: The agent's text captures the purpose of the awards but omits the specific financial amounts available for both new and continuing projects.

claims.text: Awards support exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK.
Awards cover scientific, clinical, social, and economic issues in healthcare.
Annual awards of up to £10,000 are available for new projects.
Continuing projects can receive up to £30,000 total over 3 years.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately summarizes the purpose and scope of the funding opportunity as described in the provided page text.

claims.text: The funding opportunity offers seed funding for collaborative projects.
The funding is for UK-Japan collaborative projects.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately summarizes the purpose of the Butterfield Awards, including the types of collaborations supported, the subject areas covered, and the eligible costs.

claims.text: The program supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in the UK and Japan.
The program covers scientific, clinical, social, and economic issues in healthcare.
Grants may fund travel costs.
Grants may fund conference costs.
Grants may fund publication costs.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately captures the requirement for applicants to be affiliated with an organization or institution that can receive funds, and that individuals without organizational support are not eligible, but omits all other eligibility criteria and all stated purposes for the grant.

claims.text: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds.
Individuals seeking support for personal projects are not accepted.
Individuals with organisational backing may be considered by the UK office.
Undergraduate or master's students are not supported.
Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
UK-originating projects apply to the UK office.

Grant money can be used to support festivals, workshops, performances and other events that present aspects of Japan to the UK or the UK to Japan in cultural, scientific, social, sporting and other spheres.

Grant money can be used to support exchanges between the two countries that enable participation and interaction, for instance of schools and sporting groups, artists, artisans, performers, scientists and researchers.
Grant money can be used to support collaborative projects involving UK and Japanese participants that result in new and innovative outputs for public, academic or professional presentation.
Grant money can be used to support the teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies in schools, and higher education.
Grant money can be used to support academic research, visits and exchange, where these push forward the boundaries of knowledge and understanding or involve collaboration and co-production.

records.justification: The agent's text captures some eligibility criteria related to the applicant's research record and preference for early-career applicants new to UK-Japan collaboration, but omits details about project partners, referees, and application location.

claims.text: Applicants should normally have an existing research record.
Consideration is given to practitioners, managers, and carers in health-related fields.
Consideration is given to others in health-related fields intending to establish working links or produce a publishable comparative study.
Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan.
Projects must be supported by two referees from different institutions to the project partners.
Applications should be made to the UK office.
Preference is given to those new to UK-Japan collaboration.
Preference is given to early-career applicants.
